reader.requirement: At --std 85 SORT ... USING is refused when a USING file describes a record larger than the SD's largest record (fixed SD), or a record smaller than the smallest or larger than the largest record described for a variable-length SD. Fixed versus variable is the implementor's choice for an SD with no RECORD clause or with Format 3 (§1985:II.2.1.4.3).

edition-consulted.switches: VaryingRecordInfo.BoundsEnforced via DialectBehavior.RecordContainsRangeBindsRecordSize (2002 on): at 85 the range of a Format 3 (RECORD CONTAINS m TO n) file is its record descriptions' smallest..largest, not m..n

reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: for a Format 3 SD (RECORD CONTAINS 2 TO 8, records of 3 and 6), USING a 7-byte file is refused at 85 (range 3..6, the largest record described) and accepted at 2023 (range 2..8)

reader.notes: One RecordSizeRange comparison covers both arms, and the fixed/variable classification is applied consistently. Format 3 is taken as variable, measured by its record descriptions at 85 (GR14). An SD with no RECORD clause but an ODO record is taken as fixed at its maximum. Both are implementor choices under §1985:II.2.1.4.3. I found no docs/conformance entry that names the 1985 Format-3 choice; that is a documentation check, not a rule failure.

refuter.evidence: Read SortBinder.cs#ScreenTransferRecordSizes (loops over EVERY USING file) and FileModel.cs#RecordSizeRange/VaryMin/VaryMax/ImpliesVariableFormat (ODO is not a variable-length group, so an FD/SD with no RECORD clause and an ODO record is fixed at its maximum). Probes at --std 85 (compile verdicts; EXIT 1 runs are status 35 on the absent input file): x6a SD Format 2 FROM 2 TO 8 (records 3,6), USING fixed 7 accepted (integer-3 is the largest record of the file, §1985:VII.3.8.4 GR4); x6b SD Format 2 with no FROM/TO over an ODO record (3..6 per GR5/GR6/GR7), USING fixed 2 refused; x6c USING fixed 3 and 6 accepted; x6d second USING file fixed 7 refused (each USING file checked); x6e fixed SD 6, second USING file 7 refused; x6f USING FD RECORD CONTAINS 7 over 01 X(5) vs fixed SD 6 refused (Format 1 records are 7); x6g USING FD Format 3 2 TO 8 with records 3,5 vs fixed SD 5 accepted (85 measures Format 3 by its record descriptions, GR14); x6h varying 3..5 into varying 3..6 accepted; x6i varying 3..5 into varying 4..6 refused. x6j (runtime consistency of the fixed classification): FD with an ODO record and no RECORD clause writes 6-byte padded records (12-byte file for two WRITEs) and SORT into a FROM 5 TO 6 SD returns L=6 for both, so the check's fixed-6 classification matches what the file holds. cite.py: OK  §1985:XI.4.4.3 SR3; OK  §1985:VII.3.8.4 GR6; OK  §1985:II.2.1.4.3 [it is implementor defined whether fixed length or variable length records are obtained].
